gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Growatt SPF 5000US, its $750 'lower-cost' card, is a 240 V-output-only unit that needs a separate Growatt ATS 5000T-ES transformer to power ordinary 120 V loads and carries a 2-year warranty, or that a true 120/240 V split-phase all-in-one (Sun Gold Power SPH6548P, 6.5 kW, 550 Voc) sells today for $1,035, which is $465 below the EG4 6000XP ($1,499.99) and $564 below the Growatt SPE 6000 US ($1,599).
standout_why: Compared against the cited EG4 6000XP product page, which shows no price; wildjoule.com/best-off-grid-inverter, whose footer says 'We do not display live prices', which lists the SPH6548P only with specs and doesn't cover the Growatt SPF 5000US; and storyofsolar.com's 2026 ranking, which gives undated price ranges for the EG4 ($1,499–$1,899) and Victron ($1,300–$2,200) and no figures at all for the 'Growatt SPF Series'. None of them gives dated store prices across the whole set, and none flags that the SPF 5000US outputs 240 V only. ChatGPT's own answer calls the SPF 5000US the 'lower-cost option for a small off-grid system' and says only 'verify output configuration'.
decides: It changes the budget slot. ChatGPT's $750 Growatt SPF 5000US cannot feed standard 120 V outlets without an extra transformer, and its warranty is 2 years against 5 years for the EG4. The cheapest true split-phase all-in-one with built-in MPPT priced today is the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P at $1,035 ($159 per kW against $250 per kW for the EG4 6000XP). The EG4 6000XP stays the safer main pick because its maker publishes an idle draw of 'as low as 30W (with PV)' and it lists UL 1741 with a UL 9540 system certificate. Sun Gold Power doesn't publish an idle figure for the SPH6548P, so that is its one weak point. The Growatt SPE 6000 US costs the most of the 6 kW all-in-ones at $1,599, and its only stated edge is 9,000 W of PV input against 8,000 W on the EG4.
